summary: Allow a new managed Cloud user to verify an email address and register a passkey without granting organization access from the address alone.
userImpact: New Cloud users can choose an email and passkey sign-up path separate from federated sign-in.

instructions: Deploy the signed schema-epoch compatibility release and verify its exact 0131 dual-context ledger. Drain old tenant-GUC consumers, then use the separately credentialed passkey owner to apply and verify 0132 explicit-context enforcement before applying 0133 and enabling the new flow.

configuration: Managed Cloud account identity and a working global outbound email configuration are required; the relying-party origin is the configured frontend origin.

changes: Add Cloud email-signup verification and passkey registration and authentication endpoints.

notes: The owner verifies the exact 0132 ledger and policy before applying 0133. The new pending-signup and passkey tables have no tenant membership side effects. The down migration refuses to remove populated passkey credentials.

security: Email verification establishes address control, while a verified passkey assertion authenticates the account. Matching email addresses never merge existing accounts or grant tenant membership.
Use SimpleWebAuthn server 13.3.2 to include the attestation certificate trust-anchor verification fix for GHSA-6hxq-p678-4hr2.
knownLimitations: Lost-passkey recovery requires a separate verified support process until a recovery method is deliberately introduced.
rollback: Roll the application back only to the signed compatibility release while retaining the 0133 schema. Do not remove populated passkey tables or strand passkey-only accounts; provide a verified alternate sign-in before disabling this method.
validation: Focused signup, passkey, and Cloud-session tests; PostgreSQL owner/preflight, authorization, cross-database portability, and browser acceptance remain release gates.
